items: Map Your Dating Pipeline: Draw your own pipeline by writing down every action you take between opening an app and going on a date, making it specific to your actual behavior.
Map Your Dating Pipeline: Track how much time you spend at each stage, including hidden behaviors like scrolling Instagram before swiping or rewording messages before sending.
Map Your Dating Pipeline: Calculate your conversion rates at each pipeline stage by determining how many people progress from one stage to the next out of every 100.
Map Your Dating Pipeline: Identify which stages feel productive but aren't actually producing dates, and mark them as areas needing adjustment because they're draining energy without outcomes.
Right-Size Your Work Stage: Recognize that only date scheduling and the actual date produce outcomes—everything before that is work stage preparation, not results.
Right-Size Your Work Stage: Set time limits for each work stage and stick to them, treating the apps as tools rather than entertainment that keeps you engaged forever.
Right-Size Your Work Stage: Stop measuring your success by matches or messages, and start measuring it by how many dates you actually go on each month.
Right-Size Your Work Stage: Make conscious choices about how much time to spend at each stage instead of letting the apps dictate your engagement through endless notifications.
Build Sustainable Systems: Move conversations toward scheduling dates within the first few exchanges instead of building extensive rapport through prolonged messaging that drains your energy.
Build Sustainable Systems: Design a personal system that moves people through the pipeline efficiently without requiring constant effort at every single stage.
Build Sustainable Systems: Accept that fatigue stems from poor math rather than personal flaws, and treat it as a solvable problem instead of a character deficit.
Build Sustainable Systems: Schedule dates with people you actually want to go out with at a pace you can sustain rather than matching with everyone and burning yourself out.
